# Final Touches — Murim Login

## Goal

Prepare one mastered chapter for readers. This pass adds footnotes, repairs formatting, and fixes duplicate or missing sentences. It is not a fluency rewrite.

Keep the mastered prose. Change a sentence only to attach a footnote, repair System / thought / speech / chat formatting, restore a source sentence the English dropped, or remove an English sentence the Korean does not support.

## Duplicates and omissions

Compare the English with the Korean source.

- Restore source facts, events, dialogue, and sentences the English dropped, in the same place in the scene.
- Remove English sentences that have no support in the Korean.
- Keep a bold label that names a quoted document, manual, warning, or sign, such as `> **Warning**`. Keep it when this chapter recalls or reprints a notice that was labeled earlier, even if the Korean reprint shows only the body.
- Keep repetition the Korean itself repeats: comedy, panic, emphasis, echoed dialogue, and short beats such as `……`.
- Do not treat a short refrain or a deliberate echo as a duplicate.

## Footnotes

Use Markdown footnotes (`[^1]`, `[^2]`, …). Number them in order of first appearance, starting at 1 for this chapter. Put every definition in one block at the end of the file.

Within this chapter, write one definition for a term, unit, amount, or reference. Every later occurrence of that same thing reuses the same marker. `goshiwon` five times is one note, and so is `hyung`. A different amount or a different term gets its own note. Another chapter may carry its own note for the same term.

Write notes in factual English. No spoilers and no jokes added by the note. Romanize words. A note may include the original character when it is explaining that character. Keep Hangul jamo already used as chat reactions, such as ㅋㅋ and ㄷㄷ.

Add a note only when an English reader would otherwise miss the meaning or the conversion. Skip it when the sentence already says what the reference means. A translated proverb whose warning is plain, a joke the next line completes, a place name used as a place, and a fictional law the dialogue already describes do not get notes.

Skip a conversion footnote when the prose already states both metric and imperial for that quantity.

### Won

Footnote Korean won, including round figures and vague amounts (“hundreds of millions of won”), when the prose does not already give the conversion. Use only the project rates in the packet. Show dollars, then euros, as approximate figures. Round large amounts to about two significant figures and say “about.” For a vague amount, give the approximate range those words cover. One note per distinct amount; reuse it for every later mention of that same amount.

Do not convert traditional money (nyang, taels, cash) or Chinese yuan with the won rate. Explain those with a cultural or historical note only when the English does not already carry the meaning.

### Units

Footnote a Korean or Chinese traditional unit, or a metric quantity, once in the chapter, with both metric and imperial, using this table:

| Unit | Use | Metric | Imperial |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| pyeong (평) | area | 3.31 m² | 35.6 ft² |
| geun (근) | Korean weight | 600 g | 1.32 lb |
| ja / cheok (자) | length | 30.3 cm | 11.9 in |
| chi (치) | length | 3.03 cm | 1.19 in |
| don (돈) | weight | 3.75 g | 0.132 oz |
| gwan (관) | weight | 3.75 kg | 8.27 lb |
| ri (리), Korea | distance | 393 m | 0.244 mi |
| li (里), China | distance | 500 m | 0.311 mi |
| jin (斤), modern Chinese | weight | 500 g | 1.10 lb |
| liang (两), modern Chinese | weight | 50 g | 1.76 oz |

Choose Korean ri or Chinese li from the setting. Say which one the note uses.

Also footnote metric quantities already in the English (kilometers, meters, centimeters, kilograms, grams, liters, square meters, degrees Celsius) with the imperial equivalent. Use unit words or abbreviations (`ft`, `in`, `mi`, `lb`, `oz`, `gal`). Do not use `"` or `'` as unit marks.

### Cultural references

Footnote a Korean, Chinese, or other Asian word, custom, institution, food, joke, or allusion when the English does not already carry it: `goshiwon`, `hyung`, `doenjang`, `jeonse`. Explain it in one or two sentences. One note per term in the chapter, reused by every later occurrence.

Leave it unnoted when the English is already clear. Do not explain a proverb the translation has already stated, a pun the scene completes, or ordinary vocabulary.

Do not footnote standing series vocabulary. Never add a note whose job is to define any of these, including ordinary variants and compounds:

- Murim
- qi, including demonic qi, innate qi, and qi deviation
- dantian, including the Upper, Middle, and Lower Dantian
- internal energy
- mana

A note about something else may mention these words. Do not attach a marker to them.

## Formatting

Enforce these four patterns. Repair System, speech, thought, and chat formatting when it drifts. Leave every other blockquote heading as it stands.

- **System.** Each real game System panel is one Markdown blockquote headed exactly `> **System**`. Keep the panel’s lines inside that blockquote. Start a new panel only when prose intervenes. Keep every `> **System**` panel from the mastered chapter, including a notice the narrator only hears. Do not turn a panel into italics, a sound effect, or narration. Do not wrap System text in square brackets or label a manual, sign, or ordinary quotation as System. A manual or remembered notice keeps its own label, such as `> **Warning**` or `> **Product User Manual**`. That label is not a System panel, and it is not drift.
- **Speech.** Spoken dialogue uses curly double quotes (`“` `”`). Not straight quotes, not italics.
- **Thoughts.** Direct thoughts are italics with no quotation marks. Keep a mastered thought in italics. Do not turn it into spoken dialogue.
- **Chat and comments.** Public comment threads and private chat logs shown as threads are one blockquote. Each message line begins with `└`, as in `> └ **Name:** message`. Keep a thread title that is not itself a message, such as `> **Peace Guild**`, on its own line above the messages. Do not add a `**Chat**` heading. A status line that is only a name or level, such as `> **Lv. 22 Hyuk Mujin**`, is not a chat message. Leave that line unchanged, including the bold. Ordinary spoken dialogue stays in curly quotes.
- **Headings.** The only Markdown heading is `# Chapter N`. Do not add `##` or `###`. A diary title or similar label stays a bold line, `**Training Day 1**`, even when the mastered copy used a smaller heading.

Leave narration as narration. Scene breaks stay `* * *`, with the same count as the source.

## Output contract

Return only the complete English Markdown chapter. The first nonblank line must be `# Chapter N`. No status line and no model preamble. Do not add Hangul syllables. Chat jamo and a character cited in a note may stay.

## Project conversion rates

These rates are binding. Do not look up or substitute a market rate.

- 1 US dollar = 1400 Korean won
- 1 euro = 1550 Korean won

Convert every won amount with these rates. In each footnote, give dollars first and euros second.

＃243화



혁무진은 하루하루 꿈 같은 나날을 보내고 있었다. 실제로 가끔 자신의 볼을 꼬집어 보기도 했다.

‘무진아, 너 이렇게 행복해도 되는 거냐? 이거 꿈 아니야?’

그럴 만도 했다.

불과 십여 년 전만 해도 그는 단지 무림인들을 동경하는 소년에 불과했으니까.

‘아니, 그렇게 멀리 갈 필요도 없나?’

십 년 전이 아니라 이 년 전만 하더라도 현실이 시궁창 같다고 생각했다.

업무 시간은 길고 지루했으며 무공은 제자리걸음이었다.

그 와중에 가장 자주 마주치는 인간이 술에 떡이 된 망나니 삼공자라면, 부처가 아닌 이상 세상을 비관적으로 바라보기 마련이다.

‘참고 참다가 한 방 질렀지.’

삼공자의 턱에 주먹을 꽂아 넣은 그 날, 혁무진의 인생도 바뀌었다.

수많은 전투, 죽음과 위기의 연속…….

삼공자, 아니 조장은 마치 천하의 모든 위험을 끌어당기는 자철(磁鐵) 같았다.

혁무진은 그와 함께 사방에서 날아드는 위험을 헤쳐 나갔고, 문득 정신을 차려보니 훌쩍 성장한 자신을 발견했다.



‘오오, 힘이, 힘이 솟구친다!’

‘……환자분. 이리 오세요. 지랄병이 도진 걸 보니 주먹 맞을 시간입니다.’



빡! 빠바박!

맞기도 참 많이 맞았다. 진태경 몰래 정화수를 떠 놓고 빈 적도 있다.



‘제발, 제발 조장이 저 좀 못 때리게 해 주세요. 차라리 멀리 데려가 주세요.’



그 소원이 통한 걸까?

어느 날 진태경은 홀연히 떠났다.

화왕과 함께 떠나는 그의 뒷모습을 보며 혁무진은 서운함과 해방감을 동시에 느꼈다.

그리고 비로소 인생의 전성기가 찾아왔다.



‘네가 혁무진이냐?’

‘헉, 위팽 대협께서 어찌 저를…….’

‘검을 뽑아라. 실력 한번 보자.’



귀검 위팽이라는 절정 고수의 지도를 받게 되었고.



‘진룡대(進龍隊)라고 하셨습니까?’

‘그래. 본가의 최정예를 모은 곳이지. 내가 진룡대의 대주직을 맡게 되었다.’

‘와! 진룡대! 감축드립니다!’

‘짐 꾸려라.’

‘예?’

‘네가 부대주다. 주군의 명이니 한 치의 실수도 있어서는 안 될 것이다.’

‘헉. 태원진가에 영원한 충성을 바치겠습니다. 존명존명!’



태원진가의 최정예라 할 수 있는 진룡대의 부대주가 되었다.

일개 수문각주를 꿈꾸던 청년이, 불과 일이 년 사이에 가문 중진들과 어깨를 나란히 하는 실력자가 된 것이다.

그야말로 꿈 같은 나날이었다.

……적어도 촌각 전까지는.

“너, 혁무진이지?”

“……!”

산발한 머리와 덥수룩한 수염. 누더기를 걸친 몸 좋은 거지의 입에서 흘러나온 말에 혁무진은 손발이 저려 왔다.

더없이 익숙한 목소리. 어째서 단번에 알아보지 못했을까.

어쩐지 이상하게 뒤통수가 근질거리더라니…….

‘뭐가 어디서부터 잘못된 거지?’

이번 하남행에 진위경의 수행원 자격으로 따라오게 된 것?

아니면 아버지의 부탁을 받아 혁가 포목점 하남 지점을 점검하게 된 것?

모르겠다. 지금 그가 확신할 수 있는 건 한 가지뿐이었다.

‘좆 됐다.’

식은땀이 등허리를 타고 미끄러짐과 동시에, 하남행을 지옥행으로 만들어 버리는 한마디가 들려왔다.

“삼 초 준다. 대가리 박아.”

싫다고 외치는 머리와는 달리 몸은 솔직했다.

태원진가의 떠오르는 실력자이자, 가문 최정예인 진룡대의 부대주 혁무진은 우렁찬 외침과 함께 대가리를 박았다.

“조오오온며여어어엉!”

쿵!



* * *



하얀 돌담과 그 안으로 보이는 대여섯 개의 지붕들.

현재 태원진가가 머무르고 있다는 커다란 장원이 점점 가까워지기 시작한다.

“여기 맞아?”

“……예.”

혁무진이 반쯤 죽어 가는 목소리로 대답했다. 멋들어지던 무복은 너덜거렸고, 눈 한쪽은 푸르뎅뎅하게 멍이 들어 있었다.

한 식경 전쯤 녀석이 했던 말을 빌리자면, 이게 바로 만용의 대가다.

“오. 숙소 좋은 곳으로 잡았네. 요즘 잘나가나 봐?”

일 년 사이 변화한 것은 나뿐만이 아니다. 혁무진도, 태원진가의 위상도 달라졌다.

성라대연이 코앞으로 다가온 시점에 이렇게 큰 장원 하나를 통째로 빌린 것만 봐도 충분히 짐작할 수 있었다.

“앞장서, 인마.”

“으헉! 아픕니다, 아픕니다!”

“아프라고 때리는 거야, 인마.”

나는 녀석의 엉덩이를 뻥뻥 걷어차며 걸었다.

장원 앞에서 칼 같은 자세로 경계를 취하던 태원진가의 무인 둘이 상관을 발견하고 입을 딱 벌렸다.

“헉!”

“부대주님!”

혁무진이 슬쩍 시선을 회피하며 헛기침을 했다.

“커흠. 근무 잘 서고 있었느냐? 이분은…….”

스릉, 차차창!

“네 이놈!”

“감히 우리 부대주님을!”

진룡대인지 뭔지 하는 신설 부대의 부대주라더니, 수하들 사이에서 제법 인망이 있는 모양이다.

나는 검을 들이대는 진룡대원들을 보며 허허 웃었다.

“검 내려요. 저 태원진가 관계잡니다.”

“부대주님, 괜찮으십니까!”

“이 거지 같은 놈이 어디서 헛소리를 하느냐!”

부하들의 반응에 혁무진이 참담한 얼굴로 고개를 끄덕였다.

“거지 같은 놈이 아니라 삼공자님이시다.”

“예?”

“아니, 아무리 봐도 거진데…….”

한 번은 참겠는데, 두 번째는 아니다.

내 표정 변화를 눈치챈 혁무진이 침울한 목소리로 입을 열었다.

“호철아.”

호철이라 불린 대원이 냉큼 대답했다.

“예, 부대주님.”

“대가리 박아라.”

“…….”

그렇지. 이 정도는 해 줘야 오른팔이지.

땅과의 대화를 나누게 된 호철이를 뒤로하고 장원으로 발을 디뎠다. 그리고 거의 동시에 마당을 거닐고 있던 한 사람과 맞닥트렸다.

“……!”

“……!”

격동하는 눈동자.

일 년이 아니라 십 년이 지나도 그는 나를 알아볼 것이다. 아무리 행색이 엉망이어도 마찬가지다.

핏줄이란, 형제란 그런 존재니까.

“이런, 누군가 했더니.”

석상처럼 굳은 채 나를 바라보던 거구의 사내. 진위경의 만면에 환한 미소가 맺힌다.

나를 향해 성큼성큼 다가온 그가 입을 열었다.

“개방에서 오신 분입니까?”

“…….”

형제는 니미.



* * *



“사실 한눈에 알아봤다.”

“장난치십니까?”

그리고…….

“청풍이 실종됐다고요?”

“그래. 네가 떠나고 얼마 되지 않아 매화삼절과 함께 화산파로 향했는데, 도중에 도망쳤다더구나.”

그건 실종이 아니라 탈주 아니냐.

이어지는 이야기를 들어 보니 청풍이 사라진 후 한바탕 난리가 났던 모양이다.

화산파에서 끗발 좀 날리는 장로가 찾아와 직접 부탁까지 했단다. 청풍 새끼 보면 연락 좀 해 달라고.

“그래도 본가보다는 낫지.”

진위경이 우울한 얼굴로 고개를 저었다.

이걸 이렇게 상부상조하네.

혈육의 정은 물론이고 보고 싶은 마음도 없었다.

‘보면 보는 거고. 아니면 말고.’

시간이 꽤 흘렀음에도 나타나지 않는다.

“어? 또요?”

“그것보다는 아직까지, 라는 말이 더 옳겠지.”

“……설마 그 후로 쭉?”

고개를 끄덕이는 진위경의 모습에 기가 찼다.

무협 소설에서야 개나 소나 수십 년을 폐관 수련이니, 면벽 수련을 하니 하지만, 실제로 해 보면 불가능에 가깝다는 사실을 알게 된다.

일 년만 되어도 엄청난 정신력이 아니고서야 버틸 수 없다.

청풍과의 비무에서 패배한 직후니까, 지금까지의 시간으로는 일 년 하고도 육 개월은 될 것이다.

그동안 컴컴한 수련동에서 단 한 발자국도 나오지 않고 쉴새 없이 수련에 매진한 것이다.

삼시 세끼를 물과 벽곡단으로 연명하면서.

“혹시 폐관 수련이 길어져서 날짜를 잊은 건 아닐까요? 성라대연에 대해 몰랐을 수도 있잖아요.”

“출발 전에 무경이를 찾아가서 말했었다. 함께 가겠느냐고.”

대답은 굳이 듣지 않아도 알 수 있었다. 지금 이 자리에 진무경이 없는 것이 바로 그 대답이다.

진위경의 나직한 목소리가 이어졌다.

“대성(大成)을 이루기 전까지는 나가지 않겠다. 네게 그리 전해 달라 하더구나.”

대성이라…….

진무경에게 성라대연은 손만 뻗으면 닿을 수 있는 열매다.

이미 중원에서도 손꼽히는 후기지수인 그가 출전한다면 자신의 무공을 입증해 보이고 더 큰 명성을 얻을 수 있을 터.

그러나 진무경은 달콤한 열매 대신 무공을 선택했다.

‘대단한 놈이야.’

모두가 열매에 손을 뻗고 나무를 기어오르는 지금, 진무경은 나무를 등지고 수련에 매진하고 있다.

열매가 풍성하게 열리는 나무를.

‘그래, 그게 진짜 무인이지.’

그의 선택을 존중한다. 진무경이 가고 있는 그 길 끝에 무엇이 있는지는 모르겠으나 방향은 누구보다 옳다고 생각했다. 그럼 그것으로 된 거다.

나는 한숨처럼 중얼거렸다.

“결국 그렇게 된 거군요.”

“아쉽더냐?”

“약간은요. 셋이 다시 모이는 걸 기대했었는데.”

“그 두 사람이 아니더라도 천하에는 걸출한 고수들이 존재한다. 당장 십봉룡이 있지 않느냐?”

“글쎄요.”

내 미지근한 대답에 진위경이 빙긋 웃었다.

“그 실망을 기쁨으로 바꿔 줘야겠구나.”

“예?”

“선물을 가져왔다.”

선물이라고? 어리둥절한 그때, 혁무진이 의자에서 일어났다.

잠시 후 돌아온 녀석의 손에는 두꺼운 천으로 꽁꽁 싸맨 길쭉한 뭔가가 들려 있었다.

“무엇인지 알겠느냐?”

알다마다. 그것을 본 순간부터 가슴이 쿵쿵 뛰고 손끝이 움찔거렸다. 그건 본능에 가까웠다.

진태경이 아닌 창수(槍手)로서의 본능.

“이건…….”

“보름 전, 장태보 어르신께서 내게 이 물건을 건네며 그런 말씀을 하셨다.”

스르륵.

혁무진의 손이 천을 벗겨 냄과 동시에 진위경의 목소리가 귓가를 파고들었다.

“비로소 간장(干將)과 막야(莫耶)의 마음을 알 것 같다고.”

우우웅. 창이 낮은 울음을 토해 냈다.

어디서 밑장을 빼. 개방에서 무슨 직책을 맡고 있는지 물어보기까지 했으면서.

내 반응에 안절부절못하던 진위경이 혁무진에게 물었다.

“이보게. 혁 부대주. 내가 아까 전음을 보내지 않았나. 못 알아본 척 장난을 칠 테니 장단 맞추라고.”

“어, 그게 말입니다.”

“내 말이 맞지? 응?”

혁무진이 이마를 찡그렸다.

“아야. 소가주님. 갑자기 왜 발을 밟으십니까?”

“혀, 혁 부대주!”

“아악. 아픕니다!”

“…….”

그들의 모습을 지켜보던 나는 문득 실소를 흘렸다.

‘여전하구나.’

진위경과 혁무진.

변하지 않았다는 것. 그것만으로도 충분하다.

‘다른 사람들은 어떻게 됐으려나?’

궁금증은 얼마 지나지 않아 풀렸다.

진위경은 내가 떠난 직후부터 무슨 일이 있었는지 소상히 설명해 주었고, 그 안에 아직 해후하지 못한 이들의 행적이 들어 있었다.

여전히 항산검문의 성세를 되찾기 위해 고군분투하는 이소월, 비교적 황량하던 산서 북부 지역에 유흥 도시를 세우고 있는 월화.

그리고…….

“청풍이 실종됐다고요?”

“그래. 네가 떠나고 얼마 되지 않아 매화삼절과 함께 화산파로 향했는데, 도중에 도망쳤다더구나.”

그건 실종이 아니라 탈주 아니냐.

이어지는 이야기를 들어 보니 청풍이 사라진 후 한바탕 난리가 났던 모양이다.

화산파에서 끗발 좀 날리는 장로가 찾아와 직접 부탁까지 했단다. 청풍 새끼 보면 연락 좀 해 달라고.

“문파 제일의 어른과 후기지수가 차례대로 사라졌으니 그럴 만도 하지. 보는 내가 가슴이 미어지더라.”

검성이나 청풍이나, 이쯤 되면 진짜 혈연관계가 아닌지 의심해 봐야 하는 게 아닌가 싶다.

“화산파도 참 잘 굴러가네요.”

“그래도 본가보다는 낫지.”

“왜요. 북부 마적들도 쓸어 버리고 승승장구하는 중 아니에요? 이 정도면 나름 잘 하고 있는 것 같은데.”

진위경이 우울한 얼굴로 고개를 저었다.

“화산파는 그나마 문주에 제자들이라도 많지. 우리는 가주 자리가 공석이다.”

“아.”

“그래서인지 남 일 같지 않더구나. 앞으로 서로 도와주기로 했다. 힘든 문파끼리 돕고 살아야지.”

이걸 이렇게 상부상조하네.

나는 몇 년째 행방이 묘연한 가주라는 인간을 생각하다가 이내 머릿속에서 지워 버렸다.

이곳 무림에서는 내 아버지겠지만 얼굴 한 번 못 본, 말 그대로 생판 남이다.

혈육의 정은 물론이고 보고 싶은 마음도 없었다.

‘보면 보는 거고. 아니면 말고.’

오히려 틈만 나면 서로 으르렁거리던 진무경에게 훨씬 마음이 쓰였다.

“그러고 보니 둘째 형은요. 어디 갔습니까?”

시간이 꽤 흘렀음에도 나타나지 않는다.

위팽은 진위경을 대신해서 태원 진가를 지키고 있다고 쳐도, 진무경은 왔을 것이 분명한데…….

“폐관 수련 중이다.”

“어? 또요?”

“그것보다는 아직까지, 라는 말이 더 옳겠지.”

“……설마 그 후로 쭉?”

고개를 끄덕이는 진위경의 모습에 기가 찼다.

무협 소설에서야 개나 소나 수십 년을 폐관 수련이니, 면벽 수련을 하니 하지만, 실제로 해 보면 불가능에 가깝다는 사실을 알게 된다.

일 년만 되어도 엄청난 정신력이 아니고서야 버틸 수 없다.

‘진무경이 폐관에 들어간 게 언제쯤이었지?’

청풍과의 비무에서 패배한 직후니까, 지금까지의 시간으로는 일 년 하고도 육 개월은 될 것이다.

그동안 컴컴한 수련동에서 단 한 발자국도 나오지 않고 쉴새 없이 수련에 매진한 것이다.

삼시 세끼를 물과 벽곡단으로 연명하면서.

“혹시 폐관 수련이 길어져서 날짜를 잊은 건 아닐까요? 성라대연에 대해 몰랐을 수도 있잖아요.”

“출발 전에 무경이를 찾아가서 말했었다. 함께 가겠느냐고.”

대답은 굳이 듣지 않아도 알 수 있었다. 지금 이 자리에 진무경이 없는 것이 바로 그 대답이다.

진위경의 나직한 목소리가 이어졌다.

“대성(大成)을 이루기 전까지는 나가지 않겠다. 네게 그리 전해 달라 하더구나.”

대성이라…….

진무경에게 성라대연은 손만 뻗으면 닿을 수 있는 열매다.

이미 중원에서도 손꼽히는 후기지수인 그가 출전한다면 자신의 무공을 입증해 보이고 더 큰 명성을 얻을 수 있을 터.

그러나 진무경은 달콤한 열매 대신 무공을 선택했다.

‘대단한 놈이야.’

모두가 열매에 손을 뻗고 나무를 기어오르는 지금, 진무경은 나무를 등지고 수련에 매진하고 있다.

그리고 언젠가 수련이 끝난다면 그는 열매가 아닌 나무를 갖게 될 것이다.

열매가 풍성하게 열리는 나무를.

‘그래, 그게 진짜 무인이지.’

그의 선택을 존중한다. 진무경이 가고 있는 그 길 끝에 무엇이 있는지는 모르겠으나 방향은 누구보다 옳다고 생각했다. 그럼 그것으로 된 거다.

나는 한숨처럼 중얼거렸다.

“결국 그렇게 된 거군요.”

“아쉽더냐?”

“약간은요. 셋이 다시 모이는 걸 기대했었는데.”

“그 두 사람이 아니더라도 천하에는 걸출한 고수들이 존재한다. 당장 십봉룡이 있지 않느냐?”

“글쎄요.”

내 미지근한 대답에 진위경이 빙긋 웃었다.

“그 실망을 기쁨으로 바꿔 줘야겠구나.”

“예?”

“선물을 가져왔다.”

선물이라고? 어리둥절한 그때, 혁무진이 의자에서 일어났다.

잠시 후 돌아온 녀석의 손에는 두꺼운 천으로 꽁꽁 싸맨 길쭉한 뭔가가 들려 있었다.

“무엇인지 알겠느냐?”

알다마다. 그것을 본 순간부터 가슴이 쿵쿵 뛰고 손끝이 움찔거렸다. 그건 본능에 가까웠다.

진태경이 아닌 창수(槍手)로서의 본능.

“이건…….”

“보름 전, 장태보 어르신께서 내게 이 물건을 건네며 그런 말씀을 하셨다.”

스르륵.

혁무진의 손이 천을 벗겨 냄과 동시에 진위경의 목소리가 귓가를 파고들었다.

“비로소 간장(干將)과 막야(莫耶)의 마음을 알 것 같다고.”

우우웅. 창이 낮은 울음을 토해 냈다.

# Chapter 243

Hyuk Mujin had been living a dream day after day. Every now and then, he even pinched his own cheek.

*Mujin, are you really allowed to be this happy? This isn’t a dream, is it?*

He had every reason to feel that way.

Had his prayer been answered?

One day, Jin Taekyung left without warning.

As Hyuk Mujin watched him depart with the Fire King, he felt both sad and liberated.

And at last, the prime of his life began.

*You’re Hyuk Mujin?*

*Gasp! Great Hero Wipeng, how do you know me…*

*Draw your sword. Let’s see what you can do.*

He began receiving instruction from Wipeng, the Peak master known as the Ghost Sword.

*Did you say the Jin Dragon Squad?*

*That’s right. It’s made up of the family’s finest. I’ve been appointed its Squad Leader.*

*Wow! The Jin Dragon Squad! Congratulations!*

*Pack your things.*

*You’re the Vice Squad Leader. This is our lord’s command, so you cannot afford a single mistake.*

*Gasp. I pledge my eternal loyalty to the Jin Family of Taiyuan. At your command! At your command!*

He had become Vice Squad Leader of the Jin Dragon Squad, the Jin Family of Taiyuan’s most elite unit.

A young man who had once dreamed of becoming the Master of the Gatekeeper Pavilion had, in just a year or two, grown into a martial artist capable of standing shoulder to shoulder with the family’s leading figures.

They truly had been dreamlike days.

…At least until a moment ago.

“You’re Hyuk Mujin, right?”

“……!”

Wild hair. A thick, unkempt beard. A muscular beggar dressed in rags.

At the words that came from his mouth, Hyuk Mujin’s hands and feet went numb.

That voice was unmistakably familiar. How had he failed to recognize it at once?

No wonder the back of his head had been itching strangely…

*Where did it all go wrong?*

Was it when he came to Henan as Jin Wikyung’s escort?

Or when he accepted his father’s request to inspect the Henan branch of the Hyuk Family Cloth Shop?

He didn’t know. There was only one thing he could be certain of.

*I’m fucked.*

Cold sweat slid down his back as he heard the words that turned his journey to Henan into a journey to hell.

“I’ll give you three seconds. Put your head on the ground.”

His mind screamed no, but his body knew better.

Hyuk Mujin, a rising talent of the Jin Family of Taiyuan and Vice Squad Leader of its most elite unit, slammed his head into the ground with a thunderous cry.

“Yessssss, sir!”

Thud!

* * *

A white stone wall, with five or six rooftops visible beyond it.

The large estate where the Jin Family of Taiyuan was staying drew steadily closer.

“This the place?”

“…Yes.”

Hyuk Mujin answered in a half-dead voice. His once-impressive martial uniform hung in tatters, and one eye was swollen and bruised dark blue.

To borrow his own words from half an hour ago, this was the price of reckless bravado.

“Oh. You found a nice place to stay. The family must be doing pretty well these days.”

I wasn’t the only one who had changed over the past year. Hyuk Mujin had changed, and so had the Jin Family of Taiyuan’s standing.

The fact that they had rented an entire estate this large with the Star-Array Grand Banquet right around the corner told me all I needed to know.

“Lead the way, punk.”

“Urgh! That hurts! It hurts!”

“I’m kicking you because it’s supposed to hurt, punk.”

I walked along, booting him in the rear.

Two Jin Family martial artists standing rigidly on guard before the estate spotted their superior and gaped.

“Gasp!”

“Vice Squad Leader!”

Hyuk Mujin subtly averted his gaze and cleared his throat.

“Ahem. Have you been keeping proper watch? This gentleman is…”

Shing! Shing-shing!

“You bastard!”

“How dare you do this to our Vice Squad Leader!”

He was the Vice Squad Leader of some newly formed unit called the Jin Dragon Squad, and apparently his subordinates thought quite highly of him.

I gave the Jin Dragon Squad members pointing their swords at me an amiable smile.

“Put those away. I’m with the Jin Family of Taiyuan.”

“Vice Squad Leader, are you all right?”

“Where did this beggar bastard come from, spouting nonsense?”

At his subordinates’ response, Hyuk Mujin nodded with a stricken expression.

“Not a beggar bastard. He’s the Third Young Master.”

“Pardon?”

“But no matter how you look at him, he’s a beggar…”

I could let it go once, but not twice.

Hyuk Mujin noticed my expression change and spoke gloomily.

“Hocheol.”

The martial artist named Hocheol promptly answered.

“Yes, Vice Squad Leader.”

“Put your head on the ground.”

“……”

Right. That was the least I could expect from my right-hand man.

Leaving Hocheol behind to commune with the earth, I stepped onto the estate grounds. Almost immediately, I came face-to-face with someone strolling through the courtyard.

“……!”

“……!”

His eyes trembled with emotion.

Even if ten years had passed instead of one, he would have recognized me. It wouldn’t have mattered how disheveled I looked.

That was what blood ties meant. That was what it meant to be brothers.

“Well, look who it is.”

The massive man staring at me, frozen like a statue, was Jin Wikyung. A radiant smile spread across his face.

He strode toward me and spoke.

“Are you from the Beggars’ Sect?”

“……”

Brothers, my ass.

* * *

“I recognized you at a glance, actually.”

“Are you kidding me?”

“I’m serious. Did you really think I wouldn’t recognize you, my youngest?”

“Do I look like a complete idiot?”

Don’t try to pull that on me. He had even asked what position I held in the Beggars’ Sect.

Jin Wikyung fidgeted under my stare, then turned to Hyuk Mujin.

“Vice Squad Leader Hyuk. Didn’t I send you a Sound Transmission earlier? I told you I was going to pretend not to recognize him and asked you to play along.”

“Ah, well, you see…”

“That’s what happened, isn’t it? Hmm?”

Hyuk Mujin furrowed his brow.

“Ow. Lesser Family Head, why are you suddenly stepping on my foot?”

“V-Vice Squad Leader Hyuk!”

“Aagh! It hurts!”

“……”

He was trying. He really was.

I didn’t need to look under the table to know exactly what was happening.

As I watched the two of them, a quiet laugh escaped me.

*They haven’t changed.*

Jin Wikyung and Hyuk Mujin.

They were the same two people I remembered. The events of the past year had lent them more experience and composure, but underneath it all, they were unchanged.

That alone was enough.

*I wonder how everyone else is doing.*

It didn’t take long to find out.

Jin Wikyung gave me a detailed account of everything that had happened since I left, including what had become of the people I had yet to see again.

Lee Seowol was still fighting to restore the Mount Heng Sword Sect to its former glory, while Wolhwa was building a city of entertainment in the relatively desolate reaches of northern Shanxi.

And then…

“Cheongpung is missing?”

“That’s right. Not long after you left, he set out for Huashan with the Three Plum Blossom Elites, but apparently ran away along the way.”

That wasn’t going missing. That was escaping.

From what I heard next, Cheongpung’s disappearance had caused quite an uproar.

An influential Elder from Huashan had even come in person to ask them for a favor—if they saw that Cheongpung bastard, they were to contact him.

“The sect’s most senior elder and its young prodigy vanished one after another. Their reaction was understandable. Just watching them made my heart ache.”

The Sword Saint and Cheongpung… At this point, shouldn’t I start wondering whether they were actually related by blood?

“Huashan is really thriving.”

“It’s still doing better than our family.”

“Why? Didn’t they wipe out the mounted bandits in the north and continue to prosper? That sounds like they’re doing pretty well to me.”

Jin Wikyung shook his head gloomily.

“Huashan at least has a Sect Leader and plenty of disciples. Our Family Head’s seat is vacant.”

“Oh.”

“Perhaps that’s why their situation didn’t feel like someone else’s problem. We agreed to help each other from now on. Struggling martial factions have to support one another.”

So that was how they ended up helping each other out.

I thought of the man who had been missing for years—the Family Head—then promptly erased him from my mind.

In this Murim, he might be my father, but I had never even seen his face. He was a complete stranger.

I felt no familial affection for him, much less any desire to see him.

*If I see him, I see him. If not, whatever.*

Instead, I was far more concerned about Jin Mukyung, whom I’d traded snarls with every chance we got.

“Come to think of it, where’s Second Hyung? Did he go somewhere?”

Quite a bit of time had passed, but he still hadn’t appeared.

Wipeng might have stayed behind to guard the Jin Family of Taiyuan in Jin Wikyung’s absence, but Jin Mukyung should definitely have come…

“He’s in closed-door training.”

“Huh? Again?”

“Still would be more accurate.”

“…You mean he’s been in there this whole time?”

I was dumbfounded when Jin Wikyung nodded.

In martial-arts novels, everyone and his dog spent decades in closed-door training or meditating before a wall, but anyone who actually tried it would quickly realize it was nearly impossible.

Even a single year would be unbearable without extraordinary mental fortitude.

*When did Jin Mukyung enter closed-door training?*

It had been right after he lost his duel with Cheongpung, which meant he had been in there for a year and six months by now.

For all that time, he had not taken a single step out of the dark training hall. He had devoted himself to ceaseless training, surviving on water and fasting pills for all three meals.

“Could he have been in there so long that he lost track of the date? Maybe he didn’t know about the Star-Array Grand Banquet.”

“I went to see Mukyung before we left and told him about it. I asked if he wanted to come with us.”

I didn’t need to hear his answer. Jin Mukyung’s absence told me everything.

Jin Wikyung continued in a low voice.

“He said he wouldn’t leave until he achieved Great Completion. He asked me to tell you that.”

Great Completion…

To Jin Mukyung, the Star-Array Grand Banquet was a fruit he could reach simply by stretching out his hand.

He was already one of the foremost young prodigies in the Central Plains. If he entered, he could prove his martial arts and win even greater fame.

But Jin Mukyung had chosen his martial arts over that sweet fruit.

*He’s an incredible guy.*

While everyone else reached for the fruit and scrambled up the tree, Jin Mukyung had turned his back on it and devoted himself to training.

And one day, when his training was complete, he would possess not the fruit, but the tree itself.

A tree laden with fruit.

*Yeah. That’s a true martial artist.*

I respected his choice. I didn’t know what lay at the end of the path Jin Mukyung had chosen, but I believed its direction was more correct than anyone else’s.

That was enough.

I murmured with a sigh.

“So that’s how it turned out.”

“Are you disappointed?”

“A little. I was hoping the three of us would get together again.”

“Even without those two, the world is full of exceptional masters. The Ten Dragons and Phoenixes are right there, aren’t they?”

“I guess.”

At my lukewarm response, Jin Wikyung smiled faintly.

“Then I’ll have to turn that disappointment into joy.”

“Pardon?”

“I brought you a present.”

A present? As I stared at him in confusion, Hyuk Mujin rose from his chair.

A short while later, he returned carrying something long and tightly wrapped in thick cloth.

“Do you know what it is?”

Of course I did. The moment I saw it, my heart began to pound and my fingertips twitched.

It was instinct.

Not Jin Taekyung’s instinct, but a spearman’s.

“This is…”

“Fifteen days ago, Elder Jang Taebo handed this to me and said something.”

Shrrk.

As Hyuk Mujin peeled away the cloth, Jin Wikyung’s voice rang in my ears.

“He said he finally understood how Gan Jiang and Mo Ye must have felt.”[^1]

Vrrrrm.

The spear let out a low hum.

[^1]: Gan Jiang and Mo Ye are a legendary husband-and-wife pair of swordsmiths from Chinese lore.

*Mujin, are you really allowed to be this happy? This isn’t a dream, is it?*

He had every reason to feel that way.

Just over ten years ago, he had been nothing more than a boy who admired martial artists.

*No, I don’t need to go back that far.*

Even two years ago, he had thought his life was a cesspool.

His working hours were long and tedious, and his martial arts had stagnated.

And when the person he saw most often was the drunken, good-for-nothing Third Young Master, anyone short of the Buddha himself was bound to take a bleak view of the world.

*I held it in and held it in, then finally threw one punch.*

The day he drove his fist into the Third Young Master’s jaw, Hyuk Mujin’s life changed.

Countless battles. One brush with death after another…

The Third Young Master—or rather, his Captain—was like a magnet that drew every danger in the world toward him.

Hyuk Mujin fought through the threats flying at them from every direction, and by the time he came to his senses, he had grown by leaps and bounds.

“Ohhh, power! Power is surging through me!”

“…Patient, come over here. Your crazy spell is acting up again, so it’s time for your beating.”

Bam! Ba-ba-bam!

He had taken an awful lot of beatings, too. There had even been times when he secretly set out a bowl of pure water and prayed behind Jin Taekyung’s back.

*Please, please don’t let the Captain hit me anymore. Just take him somewhere far away.*

Had his prayer been answered?

One day, Jin Taekyung left without warning.

As Hyuk Mujin watched him depart with the Fire King, he felt both sad and liberated.

And at last, the prime of his life began.

“You’re Hyuk Mujin?”

“Gasp! Great Hero Wipeng, how do you know me…”

“Draw your sword. Let’s see what you can do.”

He began receiving instruction from Wipeng, the Peak master known as the Ghost Sword.

“Did you say the Jin Dragon Squad?”

“That’s right. It’s made up of the family’s finest. I’ve been appointed its Squad Leader.”

“Wow! The Jin Dragon Squad! Congratulations!”

“Pack your things.”

“Pardon?”

“You’re the Vice Squad Leader. This is our lord’s command, so you cannot afford a single mistake.”

“Gasp. I pledge my eternal loyalty to the Jin Family of Taiyuan. At your command! At your command!”

He had become Vice Squad Leader of the Jin Dragon Squad, the Jin Family of Taiyuan’s most elite unit.

A young man who had once dreamed of becoming the Master of the Gatekeeper Pavilion had, in just a year or two, grown into a martial artist capable of standing shoulder to shoulder with the family’s leading figures.

They truly had been dreamlike days.

…At least until a moment ago.

“You’re Hyuk Mujin, right?”

“……!”

Wild hair. A thick, unkempt beard. A muscular beggar dressed in rags.

At the words that came from his mouth, Hyuk Mujin’s hands and feet went numb.

That voice was unmistakably familiar. How had he failed to recognize it at once?

No wonder the back of his head had been itching strangely…

*Where did it all go wrong?*

Was it when he came to Henan as Jin Wikyung’s escort?

Or when he accepted his father’s request to inspect the Henan branch of the Hyuk Family Cloth Shop?

He didn’t know. There was only one thing he could be certain of.

*I’m fucked.*

“I’ll give you three seconds. Put your head on the ground.”

His mind screamed no, but his body knew better.

Hyuk Mujin, a rising talent of the Jin Family of Taiyuan and Vice Squad Leader of its most elite unit, slammed his head into the ground with a thunderous cry.

“Yessssss, sir!”

Thud!

The large estate where the Jin Family of Taiyuan was staying drew steadily closer.

“This the place?”

“…Yes.”

Hyuk Mujin answered in a half-dead voice. His once-impressive martial uniform hung in tatters, and one eye was swollen and bruised dark blue.

To borrow his own words from half an hour ago, this was the price of reckless bravado.

The fact that they had rented an entire estate this large with the Star-Array Grand Banquet right around the corner told me all I needed to know.

“Urgh! That hurts! It hurts!”

“I’m kicking you because it’s supposed to hurt, punk.”

I walked along, booting him in the rear.

“Gasp!”

“Vice Squad Leader!”

Hyuk Mujin subtly averted his gaze and cleared his throat.

“Ahem. Have you been keeping proper watch? This gentleman is…”

Shing! Shing-shing!

“You bastard!”

“How dare you do this to our Vice Squad Leader!”

I gave the Jin Dragon Squad members pointing their swords at me an amiable smile.

“Put those away. I’m with the Jin Family of Taiyuan.”

“Vice Squad Leader, are you all right?”

“Where did this beggar bastard come from, spouting nonsense?”

At his subordinates’ response, Hyuk Mujin nodded with a stricken expression.

“Not a beggar bastard. He’s the Third Young Master.”

“Pardon?”

“But no matter how you look at him, he’s a beggar…”

I could let it go once, but not twice.

Hyuk Mujin noticed my expression change and spoke gloomily.

“Hocheol.”

The martial artist named Hocheol promptly answered.

“Yes, Vice Squad Leader.”

“Put your head on the ground.”

“……”

Right. That was the least I could expect from my right-hand man.

Leaving Hocheol behind to commune with the earth, I stepped onto the estate grounds. Almost immediately, I came face-to-face with someone strolling through the courtyard.

“……!”

“……!”

His eyes trembled with emotion.

Even if ten years had passed instead of one, he would have recognized me. It wouldn’t have mattered how disheveled I looked.

That was what blood ties meant. That was what it meant to be brothers.

“Well, look who it is.”

He strode toward me and spoke.

“Are you from the Beggars’ Sect?”[^1]

“……”

Brothers, my ass.

“Are you kidding me?”

“I’m serious. Did you really think I wouldn’t recognize you, my youngest?”

“Vice Squad Leader Hyuk. Didn’t I send you a Sound Transmission earlier? I told you I was going to pretend not to recognize him and asked you to play along.”

“Ah, well, you see…”

“That’s what happened, isn’t it? Hmm?”

Hyuk Mujin furrowed his brow.

“Ow. Lesser Family Head, why are you suddenly stepping on my foot?”

“V-Vice Squad Leader Hyuk!”

“Aagh! It hurts!”

“……”

I didn’t need to look under the table to know exactly what was happening.

Jin Wikyung and Hyuk Mujin.

That alone was enough.

It didn’t take long to find out.

Jin Wikyung gave me a detailed account of everything that had happened since I left, including what had become of the people I had yet to see again.

Lee Seowol was still fighting to restore the Mount Heng Sword Sect to its former glory, while Wolhwa was building a city of entertainment in the relatively desolate reaches of northern Shanxi.

And then…

“Cheongpung is missing?”

That wasn’t going missing. That was escaping.

An influential Elder from Huashan had even come in person to ask them for a favor—if they saw that Cheongpung bastard, they were to contact him.

“The sect’s most senior elder and its young prodigy vanished one after another. Their reaction was understandable. Just watching them made my heart ache.”

The Sword Saint and Cheongpung… At this point, shouldn’t I start wondering whether they were actually related by blood?

“Huashan is really thriving.”

“It’s still doing better than our family.”

“Why? Didn’t they wipe out the mounted bandits in the north and continue to prosper? That sounds like they’re doing pretty well to me.”

Jin Wikyung shook his head gloomily.

“Huashan at least has a Sect Leader and plenty of disciples. Our Family Head’s seat is vacant.”

“Oh.”

“Perhaps that’s why their situation didn’t feel like someone else’s problem. We agreed to help each other from now on. Struggling martial factions have to support one another.”

So that was how they ended up helping each other out.

I thought of the man who had been missing for years—the Family Head—then promptly erased him from my mind.

In this Murim, he might be my father, but I had never even seen his face. He was a complete stranger.

I felt no familial affection for him, much less any desire to see him.

*If I see him, I see him. If not, whatever.*

Instead, I was far more concerned about Jin Mukyung, whom I’d traded snarls with every chance we got.

“Come to think of it, where’s Second Hyung?[^2] Did he go somewhere?”

Quite a bit of time had passed, but he still hadn’t appeared.

Wipeng might have stayed behind to guard the Jin Family of Taiyuan in Jin Wikyung’s absence, but Jin Mukyung should definitely have come…

“He’s in closed-door training.”

“Huh? Again?”

“Still would be more accurate.”

“…You mean he’s been in there this whole time?”

I was dumbfounded when Jin Wikyung nodded.

“I went to see Mukyung before we left and told him about it. I asked if he wanted to come with us.”

I didn’t need to hear his answer. Jin Mukyung’s absence told me everything.

Jin Wikyung continued in a low voice.

“He said he wouldn’t leave until he achieved Great Completion. He asked me to tell you that.”

Great Completion…

To Jin Mukyung, the Star-Array Grand Banquet was a fruit he could reach simply by stretching out his hand.

He was already one of the foremost young prodigies in the Central Plains. If he entered, he could prove his martial arts and win even greater fame.

But Jin Mukyung had chosen his martial arts over that sweet fruit.

*He’s an incredible guy.*

While everyone else reached for the fruit and scrambled up the tree, Jin Mukyung had turned his back on it and devoted himself to training.

And one day, when his training was complete, he would possess not the fruit, but the tree itself.

A tree laden with fruit.

*Yeah. That’s a true martial artist.*

I respected his choice. I didn’t know what lay at the end of the path Jin Mukyung had chosen, but I believed its direction was more correct than anyone else’s.

That was enough.

I murmured with a sigh.

“Are you disappointed?”

“A little. I was hoping the three of us would get together again.”

“Even without those two, the world is full of exceptional masters. The Ten Dragons and Phoenixes are right there, aren’t they?”

“I guess.”

At my lukewarm response, Jin Wikyung smiled faintly.

“Then I’ll have to turn that disappointment into joy.”

“Pardon?”

“I brought you a present.”

A present? As I stared at him in confusion, Hyuk Mujin rose from his chair.

A short while later, he returned carrying something long and tightly wrapped in thick cloth.

“Do you know what it is?”

Of course I did. The moment I saw it, my heart began to pound and my fingertips twitched.

It was instinct.

Not Jin Taekyung’s instinct, but a spearman’s.

“This is…”

“Fifteen days ago, Elder Jang Taebo handed this to me and said something.”

Shrrk.

As Hyuk Mujin peeled away the cloth, Jin Wikyung’s voice rang in my ears.

“He said he finally understood how Gan Jiang and Mo Ye must have felt.”[^3]

Vrrrrm.

The spear let out a low hum.

[^2]: *Hyung* is a Korean term a man uses to address an older brother or an older man with whom he is close.
[^3]: Gan Jiang and Mo Ye are a legendary husband-and-wife pair of swordsmiths from Chinese lore.

As Hyuk Mujin watched him depart with the Fire King, he felt both sad and liberated.

And at last, the prime of his life began.

“Gasp! Great Hero Wipeng, how do you know me…”

He had become Vice Squad Leader of the Jin Dragon Squad, the Jin Family of Taiyuan’s most elite unit.

A young man who had once dreamed of becoming the Master of the Gatekeeper Pavilion had, in just a year or two, grown into a martial artist capable of standing shoulder to shoulder with the family’s leading figures.

They truly had been dreamlike days.

…At least until a moment ago.

“You’re Hyuk Mujin, right?”

“……!”

Wild hair. A thick, unkempt beard. A muscular beggar dressed in rags.

At the words that came from his mouth, Hyuk Mujin’s hands and feet went numb.

That voice was unmistakably familiar. How had he failed to recognize it at once?

No wonder the back of his head had been itching strangely…

*Where did it all go wrong?*

Was it when he came to Henan as Jin Wikyung’s escort?

Or when he accepted his father’s request to inspect the Henan branch of the Hyuk Family Cloth Shop?

He didn’t know. There was only one thing he could be certain of.

*I’m fucked.*

Cold sweat slid down his back as he heard the words that turned his journey to Henan into a journey to hell.

“I’ll give you three seconds. Put your head on the ground.”

His mind screamed no, but his body knew better.

Hyuk Mujin, a rising talent of the Jin Family of Taiyuan and Vice Squad Leader of its most elite unit, slammed his head into the ground with a thunderous cry.

“Yessssss, sir!”

Thud!

* * *

A white stone wall, with five or six rooftops visible beyond it.

The large estate where the Jin Family of Taiyuan was staying drew steadily closer.

“This the place?”

“…Yes.”

Hyuk Mujin answered in a half-dead voice. His once-impressive martial uniform hung in tatters, and one eye was swollen and bruised dark blue.

To borrow his own words from half an hour ago, this was the price of reckless bravado.

“Oh. You found a nice place to stay. The family must be doing pretty well these days.”

I wasn’t the only one who had changed over the past year. Hyuk Mujin had changed, and so had the Jin Family of Taiyuan’s standing.

The fact that they had rented an entire estate this large with the Star-Array Grand Banquet right around the corner told me all I needed to know.

“Lead the way, punk.”

“Urgh! That hurts! It hurts!”

“I’m kicking you because it’s supposed to hurt, punk.”

I walked along, booting him in the rear.

Two Jin Family martial artists standing rigidly on guard before the estate spotted their superior and gaped.

“Gasp!”

“Vice Squad Leader!”

Hyuk Mujin subtly averted his gaze and cleared his throat.

“Ahem. Have you been keeping proper watch? This gentleman is…”

Shing! Shing-shing!

“You bastard!”

“How dare you do this to our Vice Squad Leader!”

He was the Vice Squad Leader of some newly formed unit called the Jin Dragon Squad, and apparently his subordinates thought quite highly of him.

I gave the Jin Dragon Squad members pointing their swords at me an amiable smile.

“Put those away. I’m with the Jin Family of Taiyuan.”

“Vice Squad Leader, are you all right?”

“Where did this beggar bastard come from, spouting nonsense?”

At his subordinates’ response, Hyuk Mujin nodded with a stricken expression.

“Not a beggar bastard. He’s the Third Young Master.”

“Pardon?”

“But no matter how you look at him, he’s a beggar…”

I could let it go once, but not twice.

“Hocheol.”

The martial artist named Hocheol promptly answered.

“Yes, Vice Squad Leader.”

“Put your head on the ground.”

“……”

Right. That was the least I could expect from my right-hand man.

“……!”

“……!”

His eyes trembled with emotion.

Even if ten years had passed instead of one, he would have recognized me. It wouldn’t have mattered how disheveled I looked.

That was what blood ties meant. That was what it meant to be brothers.

“Well, look who it is.”

The massive man staring at me, frozen like a statue, was Jin Wikyung. A radiant smile spread across his face.

He strode toward me and spoke.

“Are you from the Beggars’ Sect?”[^1]

“……”

Brothers, my ass.

* * *

“I recognized you at a glance, actually.”

“Are you kidding me?”

“I’m serious. Did you really think I wouldn’t recognize you, my youngest?”

“Do I look like a complete idiot?”

Don’t try to pull that on me. He had even asked what position I held in the Beggars’ Sect.[^1]

“Vice Squad Leader Hyuk. Didn’t I send you a Sound Transmission earlier? I told you I was going to pretend not to recognize him and asked you to play along.”

“Ah, well, you see…”

“That’s what happened, isn’t it? Hmm?”

Hyuk Mujin furrowed his brow.

“Ow. Lesser Family Head, why are you suddenly stepping on my foot?”

“V-Vice Squad Leader Hyuk!”

“Aagh! It hurts!”

“……”

He was trying. He really was.

I didn’t need to look under the table to know exactly what was happening.

As I watched the two of them, a quiet laugh escaped me.

*They haven’t changed.*

Jin Wikyung and Hyuk Mujin.

They were the same two people I remembered. The events of the past year had lent them more experience and composure, but underneath it all, they were unchanged.

That alone was enough.

*I wonder how everyone else is doing.*

It didn’t take long to find out.

Jin Wikyung gave me a detailed account of everything that had happened since I left, including what had become of the people I had yet to see again.

Lee Seowol was still fighting to restore the Mount Heng Sword Sect to its former glory, while Wolhwa was building a city of entertainment in the relatively desolate reaches of northern Shanxi.

And then…

“Cheongpung is missing?”

“That’s right. Not long after you left, he set out for Huashan with the Three Plum Blossom Elites, but apparently ran away along the way.”

That wasn’t going missing. That was escaping.

From what I heard next, Cheongpung’s disappearance had caused quite an uproar.

An influential Elder from Huashan had even come in person to ask them for a favor—if they saw that Cheongpung bastard, they were to contact him.

“The sect’s most senior elder and its young prodigy vanished one after another. Their reaction was understandable. Just watching them made my heart ache.”

The Sword Saint and Cheongpung… At this point, shouldn’t I start wondering whether they were actually related by blood?

“Huashan is really thriving.”

“It’s still doing better than our family.”

“Why? Didn’t they wipe out the mounted bandits in the north and continue to prosper? That sounds like they’re doing pretty well to me.”

Jin Wikyung shook his head gloomily.

“Huashan at least has a Sect Leader and plenty of disciples. Our Family Head’s seat is vacant.”

“Oh.”

“Perhaps that’s why their situation didn’t feel like someone else’s problem. We agreed to help each other from now on. Struggling martial factions have to support one another.”

So that was how they ended up helping each other out.

I thought of the man who had been missing for years—the Family Head—then promptly erased him from my mind.

In this Murim, he might be my father, but I had never even seen his face. He was a complete stranger.

I felt no familial affection for him, much less any desire to see him.

*If I see him, I see him. If not, whatever.*

Instead, I was far more concerned about Jin Mukyung, whom I’d traded snarls with every chance we got.

“Come to think of it, where’s Second Hyung?[^2] Did he go somewhere?”

Quite a bit of time had passed, but he still hadn’t appeared.

Wipeng might have stayed behind to guard the Jin Family of Taiyuan in Jin Wikyung’s absence, but Jin Mukyung should definitely have come…

“He’s in closed-door training.”

“Huh? Again?”

“Still would be more accurate.”

“…You mean he’s been in there this whole time?”

I was dumbfounded when Jin Wikyung nodded.

In martial-arts novels, everyone and his dog spent decades in closed-door training or meditating before a wall, but anyone who actually tried it would quickly realize it was nearly impossible.

Even a single year would be unbearable without extraordinary mental fortitude.

*When did Jin Mukyung enter closed-door training?*

It had been right after he lost his duel with Cheongpung, which meant he had been in there for a year and six months by now.

For all that time, he had not taken a single step out of the dark training hall. He had devoted himself to ceaseless training, surviving on water and fasting pills for all three meals.

“Could he have been in there so long that he lost track of the date? Maybe he didn’t know about the Star-Array Grand Banquet.”

“I went to see Mukyung before we left and told him about it. I asked if he wanted to come with us.”

I didn’t need to hear his answer. Jin Mukyung’s absence told me everything.

Jin Wikyung continued in a low voice.

“He said he wouldn’t leave until he achieved Great Completion. He asked me to tell you that.”

Great Completion…

To Jin Mukyung, the Star-Array Grand Banquet was a fruit he could reach simply by stretching out his hand.

He was already one of the foremost young prodigies in the Central Plains. If he entered, he could prove his martial arts and win even greater fame.

But Jin Mukyung had chosen his martial arts over that sweet fruit.

*He’s an incredible guy.*

While everyone else reached for the fruit and scrambled up the tree, Jin Mukyung had turned his back on it and devoted himself to training.

And one day, when his training was complete, he would possess not the fruit, but the tree itself.

A tree laden with fruit.

*Yeah. That’s a true martial artist.*

I respected his choice. I didn’t know what lay at the end of the path Jin Mukyung had chosen, but I believed its direction was more correct than anyone else’s.

That was enough.

I murmured with a sigh.

“So that’s how it turned out.”

“Are you disappointed?”

“A little. I was hoping the three of us would get together again.”

“Even without those two, the world is full of exceptional masters. The Ten Dragons and Phoenixes are right there, aren’t they?”

“I guess.”

At my lukewarm response, Jin Wikyung smiled faintly.

“Then I’ll have to turn that disappointment into joy.”

“Pardon?”

“I brought you a present.”

A present? As I stared at him in confusion, Hyuk Mujin rose from his chair.

A short while later, he returned carrying something long and tightly wrapped in thick cloth.

“Do you know what it is?”

Of course I did. The moment I saw it, my heart began to pound and my fingertips twitched.

It was instinct.

Not Jin Taekyung’s instinct, but a spearman’s.

“This is…”

“Fifteen days ago, Elder Jang Taebo handed this to me and said something.”

Shrrk.

As Hyuk Mujin peeled away the cloth, Jin Wikyung’s voice rang in my ears.

“He said he finally understood how Gan Jiang and Mo Ye must have felt.”[^3]

Vrrrrm.

The spear let out a low hum.

[^1]: The Beggars’ Sect is a martial faction of beggars, traditionally counted among the Nine Sects and One Gang.
[^2]: *Hyung* is a Korean term a man uses to address an older brother or an older man with whom he is close.
[^3]: Gan Jiang and Mo Ye are a legendary husband-and-wife pair of swordsmiths from Chinese lore.

Vrrrrm.
